statuses.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO paper's per-token weight-alignment term (Eq. 2)
statuses.note: Fixed by 0cd83ff0 (fix(alignment): add WPO token weight alignment (#1025)). Verified against the PRIMARY SOURCE, not the docstring: I downloaded arXiv:2406.11827v2 and extracted Sec. 3.3, which gives Eq. (2) as w(x,y) = exp( (1/|y|) * sum_t log[ pi(y_t|x,y_<t) / sum_{v in V} pi(v|x,y_<t)^2 ] ) and states 'We use sampled alignment as the default alignment method in WPO'; Algorithm 1 says 'Calculate the alignment weight via Eq. (2)'. Current _wpo.py:74-85 computes log_denom = logsumexp(2*logits,-1) - 2*logsumexp(logits,-1) (== log sum_v p_v^2), subtracts it from per_token_logps, masked-means and exponentiates. I reproduced Eq. (2) independently in elementary form (softmax -> p_y / sum p^2 -> log -> masked mean -> exp) and got agreement to 1.5e-8 on random non-uniform logits, and confirmed the aligned/unaligned ratio varies per example (2.51 / 2.62 / 3.19 on my 3-row probe), i.e. the original defect was real and is now gone. Parity against the INSTALLED trl 1.10.0 (trainer/dpo_trainer.py:1596-1607, 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper', lse1/lse2/log_denom form) passes: packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py::test_wpo_weights_match_trl_use_weighting, whose strict xfail was removed in the same commit, passes on non-uniform randn logits (so it is not vacuous). Call site is complete: _dpo_trainer.py:1288 now passes shifted_logits, and _dpo_trainer.py:1159-1166 multiplies the per-pair loss by w_chosen*w_rejected, matching Eq. (1). DP safety preserved: I verified torch.no_grad() is honoured under torch.func.grad and vmap(grad(...)) (gradients bit-identical to an explicitly .detach()ed weight), so the weight adds no gradient path and per-record sensitivity is unchanged. Reference values in tests/test_reference_values.py were re-derived from the formula, not from the implementation (I hand-checked wpo/geometric-mean-of-aligned-token-weights = sqrt(1 * 0.125/0.78125) = 0.4). Residual noted but NOT filed as a finding because it duplicates tracked issue #862 'Upcasting the logits to fp32': _wpo.py:77-80 materialises logits.to(float32) and then 2.0*compute_logits, i.e. two extra fp32 (..., T, V) temporaries that TRL does not create; with use_weighting=True the fused logits-free path is already disabled (_dpo_trainer.py:345-349), so this is added peak memory on top of an already logits-bound branch.

statuses.title: chat-template transform: overstated coverage comments and exact-string generation-marker guards
statuses.note: Fixed by 62a96b72 (fix(alignment): support Transformers chat templates (#900)). Part (c) is fully and exactly fixed: _chat_template.py:38 now defines _GENERATION_TAG_PATTERN = re.compile(r'\{%-?\s*generation\s*-?%\}'), byte-for-byte the regex transformers 5.15.1 uses at utils/chat_template_utils.py:508, and BOTH the idempotency check (_chat_template.py:217) and _completion_mask.py:93 route through _has_generation_marker; a grep over packages/*/src finds no surviving exact-substring '{% generation %}' guard, and I confirmed a real pre-marked Hub template (HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B chat_template.jinja) round-trips unchanged. Part (a) is addressed at the prose level: the Strategy-2 comment is now 'unmarked templates with explicit assistant branches, such as ChatML' (:239-241), _wrap_gemma_shared_expression says 'Gemma-style templates' (:423), and docs/alignment/sft.md:67-72 was hedged to 'selected shared-render forms'. Coverage genuinely improved: I ran the real Hub templates through the CURRENT tree and real Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct now succeeds (new Strategy 3, _wrap_shared_content_expression) and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and Phi-3-mini and Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and SmolLM3 and gemma-2 succeed with correct assistant-only spans. CAVEAT 1 (filed as a finding): part (b)'s root cause is untouched — _chat_template.py:450-452 still uses content_pat = r'\{\{-?\s*[^}]*\bcontent\b[^}]*-?\}\}' and bails on len(content_matches) != 1; on the real google/gemma-3-1b-it template that regex still matches exactly two expressions, "{{ message['content'] | trim }}" and '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}', so get_training_chat_template still raises, and the canonical shared-expression ChatML still raises — while the new test at tests/data/test_chat_template.py:379-383 labels its parameters 'gemma-3-1b-it' and 'shared-chatml' while actually exercising synthetic stand-ins that do not have those properties. CAVEAT 2 (filed as a finding): the new validator _generation_block_marks_only_assistant checks only span membership and never checks that the transformed template renders the same text as the original, and the insertion changes the rendering under Jinja trim_blocks on 3 of the 9 real Hub templates the transform accepts.

statuses.title: Correct alignment loss and data-preparation contracts (umbrella)
statuses.note: Child #826/OPQ-348 is fixed-verified against the primary source and against installed TRL. Child #827/OPQ-349 is fixed-with-caveats: its (a) and (c) parts are done, its (b) part (real gemma-3-1b-it rejection) survives with the root cause untouched, and the fix introduced a template-render-fidelity gap and a misdiagnosing per-row error that are filed as findings below. Closing the umbrella therefore overstates completion of the data-preparation half.

findings.title: get_training_chat_template silently changes the rendered conversation text (Jinja trim_blocks eats the newline after the wrapped expression)
findings.claim: The transform inserts the Jinja BLOCK tags {% generation %} / {% endgeneration %} around a {{ ... }} expression. transformers compiles chat templates with trim_blocks=True (transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py::_compile_jinja_template), so a newline immediately following a block tag is deleted from the output. Whenever the wrapped expression is followed in the template source by a literal newline — the normal shape of a multi-line, non-whitespace-controlled template — inserting {% endgeneration %} there removes a newline the original template emitted. The only acceptance gate, _generation_block_marks_only_assistant (:469-520), inspects the CONTENT of the generation spans ('assistant probe in generated', 'user probe not in generated', 'system probe not in generated') and never compares the transformed render against the original render, so the change passes validation.
findings.failure_scenario:
A user runs DPTrainer with SFTConfig(assistant_only_loss=True) on any of these real Hub tokenizers. _sft_trainer.py:426-428 permanently overwrites processing_class.chat_template with the transformed template, and every row is then tokenized from it. I rendered the original and the transformed template with the same 4-message conversation through transformers' own _render_with_assistant_indices and got, for HuggingFaceH4/zephyr-7b-beta, TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 and stabilityai/stablelm-2-zephyr-1_6b, identically: original '<|user|>
U1</s>
<|assistant|>
A1</s>
<|user|>
U2</s>
<|assistant|>
A2</s>
' vs training '<|user|>
U1</s>
<|assistant|>
A1</s><|user|>
U2</s>
<|assistant|>
A2</s>' — one turn-separator newline dropped after every assistant turn, and the trailing newline dropped. The model is therefore fine-tuned on token sequences that the model's canonical chat template never produces; at inference time a freshly loaded tokenizer emits the newline the model was trained never to see. The assistant mask itself stays correct, so nothing warns.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_chat_template.py:326-332 — `return (template[:abs_start] + _GEN_START + template[abs_start:abs_end] + _GEN_END + template[abs_end:])` with _GEN_START/_GEN_END the block tags defined at :36-37.

packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_chat_template.py:469-520 — the validator only builds `generated = ''.join(rendered[start:end] ...)` and asserts probe membership; there is no comparison of `rendered` against the untransformed template's rendering.
transformers 5.15.1 utils/chat_template_utils.py::_compile_jinja_template compiles with trim_blocks=True, which is what deletes the newline after {% endgeneration %}.

Reproduced on the real templates: transformed zephyr-7b-beta template contains "...{% elif message['role'] == 'assistant' %}\n{% generation %}{{ '<|assistant|>\\n'  + message['content'] + eos_token }}{% endgeneration %}\n{% endif %}..."; rendering original vs transformed differs as quoted in the failure scenario (script: scratchpad/repro_trim.py, scratchpad/probe_all.py).

3 of the 9 real Hub templates that the transform currently accepts show the divergence (zephyr-7b-beta, TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, stablelm-2-zephyr-1_6b); llama3, gemma-2, Qwen2.5, Phi-3, Mistral-v0.3 and SmolLM3 are unaffected because they are single-line or fully whitespace-controlled.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:426-428 — `processing_class.chat_template = get_training_chat_template(processing_class)` makes the transformed template the one that actually tokenizes training data.
findings.fix_sketch: Make _generation_block_marks_only_assistant reject any candidate whose full rendered string differs from the untransformed template's rendering for the same probe messages (it already renders both shapes; add `rendered_base == rendered_candidate`). Independently, emit whitespace-neutral markers — e.g. wrap as `{%+ generation +%}` / `{%+ endgeneration +%}`, or re-append the swallowed newline — so the insertion is text-preserving by construction rather than by validation.

findings.title: apply_chat_template_with_mask reports a per-row truncation as a chat-template misconfiguration and aborts the whole dataset map
findings.claim: 62a96b72 replaced `if not assistant_masks:` with `if not _has_assistant_tokens(assistant_masks):` (:114, helper at :136-142), so an all-zero mask now raises. But the function already validated the template up front at :93. By the time :114 runs, a False result can only mean 'this particular conversation rendered no assistant tokens', which for the trainer's call is caused by truncation, not by the template. The error text nonetheless asserts 'This means the chat template does not carry the {% generation %} / {% endgeneration %} markers' and tells the user to install markers that are already installed.
findings.failure_scenario: SFTConfig(assistant_only_loss=True, max_length=N) calls apply_chat_template_with_mask(..., max_length=N, truncation=True) from _sft_trainer.py:455-461 inside dataset.map. Any single conversation whose system+user prefix exceeds N tokens truncates before the first assistant token, so assistant_masks is all zeros and the call raises ConfigurationError — aborting preparation of the entire dataset with a diagnosis that points at the tokenizer instead of at max_length. Reproduced end to end with the real Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct tokenizer: get_training_chat_template succeeds, the untruncated conversation yields completion_mask.sum() == 16, and the same conversation with max_length=64, truncation=True raises 'ConfigurationError: apply_chat_template_with_mask: the tokenizer returned no assistant-token mask. This means the chat template does not carry the ...markers...'. Before 62a96b72 the same row passed with an all-zero mask (nll_loss clamps its divisor to 1, so it contributed a 0.0 loss rather than a NaN), so the change trades a silently useless row for a hard abort with the wrong remedy.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_completion_mask.py:93-103 — the template-level guard already ran and passed before line 114 is reached.

packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_completion_mask.py:114-124 — `if not _has_assistant_tokens(assistant_masks): raise ConfigurationError(... 'This means the chat template does not carry the ... markers' ...)`.

packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:455-461 — `apply_chat_template_with_mask(processing_class, example[chat_col], max_length=max_length, truncation=max_length is not None)` inside the dataset.map at :436-441.
Reproduced with the real Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct tokenizer: untruncated mask sum = 16; `max_length=64, truncation=True` -> ConfigurationError with the quoted text.
git show 62a96b72 -- .../_completion_mask.py: the old guard was `if not assistant_masks:`, which is True only for None/empty, so an all-zero list previously passed.
findings.fix_sketch: Split the two conditions. Keep the template check at :93 as the ConfigurationError. For an empty mask on a rendered row, raise a distinct error whose message names truncation/max_length and the offending conversation (or return the row with an all-zero mask and let the caller drop it), so a single over-long conversation does not abort dataset preparation with a misdirected remedy. The trainer can then filter or report the row.

findings.title: Real gemma-3-1b-it and canonical shared-expression ChatML are still rejected, while a new test labels its parameters with those exact names
findings.claim: OPQ-349(b) named a specific root cause: content_pat matches two expressions in the real gemma-3 template, so the `len(content_matches) != 1` bail rejects it. That regex and that bail are unchanged at _chat_template.py:450-452. The fix took the documentation route instead, which the OPQ fix sketch allowed — but the commit simultaneously added a parametrized test whose ids are 'meta-llama-3-8b-instruct', 'gemma-3-1b-it' and 'shared-chatml' while the actual parameters are _LLAMA_3_TEMPLATE (genuinely the real Llama-3 template), _GEMMA_INLINE_TEMPLATE (a synthetic one-line `{% set role = 'model' if ... %}` template that is not gemma-3-1b-it and lacks its second content expression) and _CHATML_TEMPLATE (which has an explicit `{% elif message['role'] == 'assistant' %}` branch, i.e. it is not the shared-expression ChatML the finding named).
findings.failure_scenario: A maintainer reads a green `test_representative_templates_render_assistant_only[gemma-3-1b-it]` and concludes the real Gemma-3 template is supported. It is not: a user who calls DPTrainer(SFTConfig(assistant_only_loss=True)) with google/gemma-3-1b-it — a family AGENTS.md lists as supported — gets ConfigurationError('could not identify and validate an assistant-only render path'). Same for a tokenizer carrying the canonical shared-expression ChatML template. I confirmed the exact cause on the real gemma-3 template: content_pat.finditer returns ["{{ message['content'] | trim }}", '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}'], the assistant->model branch mapping matches, and _wrap_gemma_shared_expression returns None; all four other strategies also return None.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/tests/data/test_chat_template.py:379-383 — `@pytest.mark.parametrize('template', [_LLAMA_3_TEMPLATE, _GEMMA_INLINE_TEMPLATE, _CHATML_TEMPLATE], ids=['meta-llama-3-8b-instruct', 'gemma-3-1b-it', 'shared-chatml'])`.

packages/opaque-alignment/tests/data/test_chat_template.py:74-81 — _GEMMA_INLINE_TEMPLATE is a one-line synthetic template; :40-48 — _CHATML_TEMPLATE carries an explicit `{% elif message['role'] == 'assistant' %}` branch.

packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/data/_chat_template.py:450-452 — `content_pat = re.compile(r"\{\{-?\s*[^}]*\bcontent\b[^}]*-?\}\}")` / `if len(content_matches) != 1: return None`, unchanged by 62a96b72.

Running the real google/gemma-3-1b-it chat_template and the canonical shared-expression ChatML through the current tree: both raise ConfigurationError('could not identify and validate an assistant-only render path'); instrumenting the helpers shows content matches == ["{{ message['content'] | trim }}", '{{ raise_exception("Invalid content type") }}'] and all of _wrap_assistant_content / _wrap_shared_content_expression / _wrap_gemma_shared_expression / _wrap_shared_or_clause returning None.

By contrast the real Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct, gemma-2-2b-it, Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct, Phi-3-mini-4k-instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 and SmolLM3-3B templates all succeed with correct assistant-only spans.
findings.fix_sketch: Either rename the ids to describe the shapes actually exercised ('shared-set-content', 'inline-role-mapping', 'explicit-assistant-branch'), or make the named templates real: exclude `raise_exception(...)` expressions from content_pat (e.g. require the expression to reference `message` or a role/content variable) so the real gemma-3 template's single renderable content expression is found, and add a shared-expression ChatML strategy. If the real templates stay unsupported, say so explicitly in docs/alignment/sft.md next to the Gemma mention.

findings.title: language_modeling_collator(completion_only_loss=True) now silently supervises the full sequence for rows that carry no completion_mask
findings.claim: 08d8b1dc inverted the maskless-row behaviour of the public collator. Before, a row without completion_mask had all real tokens set to -100 under completion_only_loss=True (fail-closed: no prompt tokens are ever supervised). Now the `if has_completion_mask and cm is not None` branch (:147) simply does not fire, the labels stay a full copy of input_ids, and the `elif has_completion_mask` branch (:158-161) additionally reports that row's completion_mask as all ones — asserting those prompt tokens ARE completion tokens.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller using the exported opaque.alignment.sft.collator.language_modeling_collator directly (not through DPTrainer) asks for completion_only_loss=True and feeds a batch in which some or all rows lack completion_mask — e.g. a hand-assembled mixed dataset, or a preprocessing step that dropped the column. Reproduced: `language_modeling_collator(pad_token_id=0, max_length=16, completion_only_loss=True)([{'input_ids':[1,2,3]},{'input_ids':[4,5,6]}])` returns labels [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] (full supervision, and no completion_mask key at all); the mixed case `[{'input_ids':[1,2,3],'completion_mask':[0,1,1]},{'input_ids':[4,5,6]}]` returns labels [[-100,2,3],[4,5,6]] and completion_mask [[0,1,1],[1,1,1]]. The prompt tokens the caller asked to exclude are trained on, and the returned mask claims they are completions. DPTrainer itself is guarded (_sft_trainer.py:406-417 raises when completion_only_loss=True has neither a prompt-completion dataset nor a completion_mask), so this is a defect of the public primitive rather than the default trainer path.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/sft/collator/_language_modeling.py:147-161 — `if has_completion_mask and cm is not None: ... elif has_completion_mask: completion_mask_t[i, :seq_len] = 1` with no branch that honours _completion_only_loss for a maskless row.
git show 08d8b1dc: the removed code was `else: if self._completion_only_loss: labels_t[i, :seq_len] = _IGNORE_INDEX` and `elif self._completion_only_loss: labels_t[i, :seq_len] = _IGNORE_INDEX`.
Reproduced against the current tree through the public facade opaque.alignment.sft.collator.language_modeling_collator, outputs as quoted in the failure scenario.
packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:406-417 — the trainer-level guard that keeps the default path off this branch.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the TRL-matching default but make it explicit rather than silent: when _completion_only_loss is set and a row supplies no completion_mask, either raise (the collator already knows both facts) or emit a one-shot warning naming the row index, instead of flipping that row to full supervision and reporting an all-ones completion_mask. At minimum, do not fabricate completion_mask=1 for tokens the caller never marked as completions.

findings.title: mpo_combine changed its documented exception type from KeyError to ConfigurationError (a ValueError) in a non-breaking commit
findings.claim: 7b26f655 (feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy (#760)) replaced `raise KeyError(...)` with `raise ConfigurationError(...)` in the public mpo_combine. ConfigurationError derives from OpaqueError and ValueError (packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27) — it is NOT a KeyError — so existing `except KeyError:` handlers around mpo_combine stop catching. The taxonomy's own docstring markets this property ('preserve familiar Python error relationships'), which it does for the ValueError/TypeError/RuntimeError swaps elsewhere in the same commit but not for this one.
findings.failure_scenario: User code that composes MPO heads and guards the weights/losses key mismatch with `except KeyError:` — the contract the previous docstring promised ('Raises: KeyError: If weights names a key that is absent from losses') — now propagates an uncaught ConfigurationError. The change shipped under a `feat` title without the `!` marker that AGENTS.md requires for breaking changes, so it does not appear as a breaking change in the changelog for the release line that contains it.
evidence: packages/opaque-alignment/src/opaque/api/alignment/dpo/loss/_mpo.py:58 and :70 — `raise ConfigurationError(...)` where the pre-delta code raised KeyError (git show 7b26f655 -- .../_mpo.py).
packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/exceptions/__init__.py:27 — `class ConfigurationError(OpaqueError, ValueError)`; no KeyError in the MRO.
git show 7b26f655 diff of _mpo.py also rewrites the docstring from 'Raises: KeyError' to 'Raises: ConfigurationError', confirming the contract change was intentional and undeclared as breaking.
Commit subject is `feat(exceptions): add public exception taxonomy (#760)` — no `!` and no BREAKING CHANGE footer.
findings.fix_sketch: Either make the mpo_combine failure a type that is still a KeyError (e.g. a dedicated `class MissingLossKeyError(ConfigurationError, KeyError)` in the taxonomy, mirroring how ConfigurationError keeps ValueError) or record the change as breaking in the changelog for the release that contains 7b26f655.
